peer_results.rationale: AMD's Item 1 disclosures focus on global workforce headcount (28,000 employees) and employee advancement/development programs (tuition reimbursement, leadership training), but do not provide specific demographic statistics on gender or underrepresented minority representation comparable to Intel's diversity workforce demographics.

AVGO's Item 1 disclosures focus on CEO background and voluntary attrition rates (2.9% to 6.2%), which relate to executive leadership history and employee retention metrics rather than the specific diversity workforce demographics and representation statistics disclosed by Intel.

comparisons.peer_topic: Board of Directors gender and ethnic diversity composition
comparisons.peer_summary: As of August 29, 2024, the Board comprised five men and four women, including one Asian member, one African-American member, and seven White members.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Micron disclose specific demographic composition data related to diversity in Item 1, though Intel focuses on employee/leadership demographics while Micron focuses on Board composition. Intel reports that underrepresented minorities comprised 8.7% of its US senior leadership positions. Micron reports its Board diversity, stating that as of August 29, 2024, the Board included one Asian member, one African-American member, and seven White members. Both provide specific headcount or percentage breakdowns of diverse representation within their organizational structures.

sentences.text: Underrepresented minorities [footnote 3: Underrepresented minority population includes all regular Intel employees but does not include Mobileye and other non-integrated subsidiaries employees.] , including Black/African American employees, Hispanic, and Native American employees, represented 17.8% of our US employees and 8.7% of our US senior leadership positions.
In addition, as of August 29, 2024, based on self-identification, one member of our Board of Directors is Asian, one member is African-American, and seven members are White.

comparisons.peer_summary: As of the end of fiscal year 2024, the global workforce was 79% male, 20% female, and 1% not declared, with 6% of the US workforce composed of Black or African American and Hispanic or Latino employees.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and NVIDIA report specific quantitative demographic breakdowns of their workforce in Item 1, covering gender and underrepresented minority representation. Intel reports that women represented 27.9% of global employees and 25.3% of technical positions, while underrepresented minorities comprised 17.8% of US employees. NVIDIA reports that its global workforce was 20% female and that 6% of its US workforce was composed of Black or African American and Hispanic or Latino employees. Both disclosures provide granular headcount percentages for diversity metrics.

As of the end of fiscal year 2024, our global workforce was 79% male, 20% female, and 1% not declared, with 6% of our workforce in the United States composed of Black or African American and Hispanic or Latino employees.

comparisons.peer_summary: Qualcomm focuses DEI efforts on inspiring innovation through inclusive culture, recruiting diverse talent, and identifying strategic partners, supported by global employee network groups and engagement with diverse communities.
comparisons.comparison: Intel and Qualcomm both address Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) as a structural component of their human capital management in Item 1. Intel provides specific statistical outcomes of its diversity efforts, such as 27.9% female global employees. Qualcomm focuses on the strategic framework driving these outcomes, stating that DEI efforts are focused on 'inspiring innovation through an inclusive and diverse culture' and 'expanding our efforts to recruit world-class diverse talent,' supported by global employee network groups.

Population includes all regular Intel employees but does not include Mobileye and other non-integrated subsidiaries employees.] , and 25.3% of our technical positions.
We believe that a diverse workforce is important to our success, and we continue to focus on making Qualcomm a great place to work for everyone, including women and underrepresented populations.

Our recent efforts have been focused in three areas: inspiring innovation through an inclusive and diverse culture; expanding our efforts to recruit world-class diverse talent; and identifying strategic partners to accelerate our programs.
